title: Anthropic IPO: The AI World Wonder
text: Byron Deeter, Sameer Dholakia, David Cowan, Grace Ma, Alex Yuditski & Sam BondySix months before Dario Amodei wrote Machines of Loving Grace in 2024, Bessemer circulated its first investment memo on Anthropic calling it “a generational AI infrastructure” business. Since then, we backed every subsequent round of Anthropic’s funding. And what’s really promising is that this is just the beginning of Anthropic’s story and the opportunity ahead.Byron Deeter and Sameer Dholakia led with conviction that outpaced Silicon Valley’s consensus. It was a time when most still underestimated AI’s potential to transform the world for the better, as Dario wrote in his seminal essay. We believe AI hold the promise to transform biology and human health, drive innovation, entrepreneurship, and scientific breakthroughs, and reinvent how people and global enterprises operate and collaborate.Their trajectory has been astonishing to witness: a-once-fringe frontier lab, convicted in their early beliefs that artificial intelligence must always be helpful, honest, and harmless, has grown into a global enterprise reimagining nearly every sector and slice of the economy.Anthropic was our choice in the foundational model market because its enterprise-first strategy had the makings of a business that could get as big as the hyperscalers, built on a foundation of safety and trust that enterprises require. Anthropic moved first to serve developers with code generation and agentic coding, and its early partnerships with AWS, Google, and others built durable distribution moats. “Awe-inspiring” and “unprecedented” are words our investors have used to describe Anthropic’s meteoric run for the past two-and-a-half years.The industry is rapidly deploying AI across all industries, and with that Anthropic’s focus on responsible AI has only widened with time. As investors, we often say that tone starts at the top, and that success is measured not just by the scale and speed of growth but by how well a business stays true to its mission and values along the way. At every stage, Anthropic has held to its original mission: the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. Dario, Daniela, and the management team continue to offer stable and consistent leadership as AI Giants play a pivotal role in steering the pace of the frontier.Anthropic has always aligned with our ethos: Bessemer backs founders building foundational technologies that reshape how people live and work, from the steel beams that raised modern skylines to the World Wide Web, cloud computing, and the frontier of science.The incredible vision Anthropic’s co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, along with Tom Brown, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, Chris Olah, and Jack Clark, set from the beginning deepened our belief that Anthropic would become the infrastructure of progress in the AI era.Anthropic is the largest bet in our history, and one of the most astonishing businesses we’ve ever seen. Their IPO is a punctuation mark in the history of both humanity and technology—and everyone at Bessemer is proud to be part of Anthropic’s past, present, and future.ContributorsByron DeeterPartnerByron Deeter is a leading investor in AI, Cloud, Frontier Technology, and the Business of Sports. He co-authored Bessemer’s iconic AI 100, the Bessemer Forbes Cloud 100, the BVP Nasdaq Emerging Cloud Index, and Bessemer’s STRIVE program for executive health and wellness. Byron works closely alongside many of the best founders in the AI and cloud worlds, with 26 of Byron’s investments currently valued above $1 billion each, including 13 IPOs and counting.Byron first raised a Series A with Bessemer back in 2000, as CEO and founder of Trigo Technologies. His company grew to be one of the first global SaaS companies, reaching profitability and was successfully sold to IBM. Byron foresaw that cloud computing would not only change the way people built new technologies but also how The Cloud would systematically run the world. In 2005, Byron returned to Bessemer, this time to help lead the firm’s global cloud practice.Byron graduated with honors from The University of California, Berkeley, where he met his then college sweetheart and now wife. Byron is a perennial Midas List investor, past Chairman of the National Venture Capital Association, partner/owner of the San Francisco 49ers and Leeds United, as well as an active board member/advisor to numerous causes including the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Foundation, U.C. Berkeley Foundation, Pledge 1% and Cal Rugby. He accelerated the company’s growth and led SendGrid through a successful IPO in 2017 and subsequent acquisition by leading cloud communications platform Twilio for approximately $3 billion in early 2019. Before joining SendGrid, Sameer served as GM of the Cloud Platforms Group at Citrix, which he joined following its acquisition of his first startup, VMLogix.Sameer earned a B.A. in economics and a M.A. in organizational studies from Stanford University.
